arxiv-2108-13852.title: Cross-fertilising extra gauge boson searches at the LHC
arxiv-2108-13852.creator: Jack Y. Araz, ​​, Mariana Frank, ​​, Benjamin Fuks, ​​, Stefano Moretti, ​ and Özer Özdal
arxiv-2108-13852.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Jack Y. Araz, ​​, Mariana Frank, ​​, Benjamin Fuks, ​​, Stefano Moretti, ​ and Özer Özdal. For the purpose of cross-fertilising currently separate experimental approaches, we connect results of LHC analyses attempting to access the properties of additional W ′ W^{\prime} and Z ′ Z^{\prime} bosons from Drell-Yan processes.

arxiv-2109-01977.title: A weak type estimate for regular fractional sparse operators
arxiv-2109-01977.creator: Ji Li, Chung-Wei Liang, Chun-Yen Shen
arxiv-2109-01977.description: Abstract In this note the weak type estimates for fractional integrals are studied. More precisely, we adapt the arguments of Domingo-Salazar, Lacey, and Rey to obtain improvements for the end point weak type estimates for regular fractional sparse operators. 1 Introduction Let M denote the Hardy–Littlewood maximal function. The Muckenhoupt–Wheeden Conjecture stems from vector-valued estimates for the maximal function.

arxiv-2210-07426.title: Skill-Based Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Reward Matching
arxiv-2210-07426.creator: Ademi AdenijiUC Berkeley, Amber XieUC BerkeleyPieter AbbeelUC Berkeley
arxiv-2210-07426.description: Abstract While unsupervised skill discovery has shown promise in autonomously acquiring behavioral primitives, there is still a large methodological disconnect between task-agnostic skill pretraining and downstream, task-aware finetuning. We present Intrinsic Reward Matching (IRM), which unifies these two phases of learning via the skill discriminator , a pretraining model component often discarded during finetuning.

arxiv-2302-05374.title: LCDnet: A Lightweight Crowd Density Estimation Model for Real-time Video Surveillance
arxiv-2302-05374.creator: Muhammad Asif Khan, Hamid Menouar, Ridha Hamila
arxiv-2302-05374.description: Abstract Automatic crowd counting using density estimation has gained significant attention in computer vision research. As a result, a large number of crowd counting and density estimation models using convolution neural networks (CNN) have been published in the last few years. These models have achieved good accuracy over benchmark datasets.

arxiv-2306-17755.title: An Improved Deterministic Algorithm for the Online Min-Sum Set Cover Problem
arxiv-2306-17755.creator: Mateusz Basiak, Marcin Bienkowski, Agnieszka Tatarczuk
arxiv-2306-17755.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mateusz Basiak, Marcin Bienkowski, Agnieszka Tatarczuk. We study the online variant of the Min-Sum Set Cover ( Mssc ) problem, a generalization of the well-known list update problem. In the Mssc problem, an algorithm has to maintain the time-varying permutation of the list of n n elements, and serve a sequence of requests R 1 , R 2 , … , R t , … R_{1},R_{2},\dots,R_{t},\dots . Each R t R_{t} is a subset of elements of cardinality at most r r .

arxiv-2310-14759.title: Anomalous kinetics of a multi-species reaction-diffusion system: effect of random velocity fluctuations E-mail: hnatic@saske.sk E-mail: matej.kecer@student.upjs.sk E-mail: tomas.lucivjansky@upjs.sk
arxiv-2310-14759.description: Abstract Reaction-diffusion systems, which consist of the reacting particles subject to diffusion process, constitute one of the common examples of non-linear statistical systems. In low space dimensions d ≤ 2 d\leq 2 the usual description by means of kinetic rate equations is not sufficient and the effect of density fluctuations has to be properly taken into account.

arxiv-2402-13349.title: Aria Everyday Activities Dataset
arxiv-2402-13349.creator: Zhaoyang Lv, Nicholas Charron, Pierre Moulon, Alexander Gamino, Cheng Peng, Chris Sweeney
arxiv-2402-13349.description: Abstract We present Aria Everyday Activities (AEA) Dataset, an egocentric multimodal open dataset recorded using Project Aria glasses. AEA contains 143 daily activity sequences recorded by multiple wearers in five geographically diverse indoor locations. Each of the recording contains multimodal sensor data recorded through the Project Aria glasses.

arxiv-2404-18988.title: Markovian Transformers for Informative Language Modeling
arxiv-2404-18988.creator: Scott Viteri, Max Lamparth, Peter Chatain, Clark Barrett
arxiv-2404-18988.description: Abstract Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning often fails to faithfully reflect a language model’s underlying decision process. We address this by making CoT text causally essential in a “Markovian” language model, factoring next-token prediction through an intermediate CoT and training it to predict future tokens independently of the original prompt.

arxiv-2410-14464.title: Electrocardiogram–Language Model for Few-Shot Question Answering with Meta Learning
arxiv-2410-14464.creator: Jialu Tang, Tong Xia, Yuan Lu, Cecilia Mascolo, Aaqib Saeed
arxiv-2410-14464.description: Abstract Electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation requires specialized expertise, often involving synthesizing insights from ECG signals with complex clinical queries posed in natural language. The scarcity of labeled ECG data coupled with the diverse nature of clinical inquiries presents a significant challenge for developing robust and adaptable ECG diagnostic systems.

arxiv-2509-10049.title: Universal Driven Critical Dynamics near the Boundary
arxiv-2509-10049.creator: Yu-Rong Shu, Shuai Yin
arxiv-2509-10049.description: Abstract The celebrated Kibble-Zurek mechanism (KZM) describes the scaling of physical quantities when external parameters sweep through a critical point. Boundaries are ubiquitous in real systems, and critical behaviors near the boundary have attracted extensive research. Different boundary universality classes, including ordinary, special, extraordinary, and surface transitions, have been identified. However, the driven critical dynamics near boundaries remains unexplored.

pmc-12397704.title: Comparison of [68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04 and [18F]FDG PET/CT for detection of bone metastases of lung cancer
pmc-12397704.creator: Ji Wu, Yang Meng, Qinyao Li, Chunyin Zhang, Guohao Jiang
pmc-12397704.description: BackgroundBone metastases of lung cancer typically indicate disease progression and poor prognosis. Early and accurate detection is crucial for staging, treatment planning, and prognostic evaluation. This study aimed to compare the diagnostic value of gallium 68-labeled fibroblast-activation protein inhibitor-04 ([68Ga]Ga-FAPI-04) and fluorine 18-labeled fluorodeoxyglucose ([18F]FDG) positron-emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) imaging in detecting bone metastases in lung cancer.

pmc-12448334.title: Molecular basis for the activation of the bitter taste receptor TAS2R14 by Ritonavir
pmc-12448334.creator: Jiao Wen, Xinyi Ma, Xinyi Zhou, R. Charles Kissell, Yongcheng Lu, Yukyoung Kim, Young Seo Lee, Alice Lee, Shurui Chen, Keman Xu, Leigh D. Plant, Meng Cui
pmc-12448334.description: Ritonavir is a protease inhibitor used in combination with other antiretroviral drugs to treat HIV, especially in children. It enhances the effectiveness of these drugs by inhibiting the cytochrome P450-3A4 enzyme, thereby increasing their bioavailability. Ritonavir is also being investigated for cancer treatment due to its mechanism of action.

pmc-12566324.title: Challenges and Potential of Antibody–Drug Conjugates as Prospective Tuberculosis Therapeutics
pmc-12566324.creator: Kenneth W Foreman, Hui-Chen Foreman, Kaixia Mi
pmc-12566324.description: Tuberculosis (TB), primarily caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), remains a leading cause of infectious disease mortality worldwide. Global TB control efforts face several hurdles, including the lack of a broadly effective vaccine, limited sensitivity of current diagnostics, particularly for paucibacillary and extrapulmonary TB, and significant adverse effects associated with prolonged small-molecule drug regimens.

pmc-12685991.title: Morpheme knowledge is shaped by information available through orthography
pmc-12685991.creator: Maria Korochkina, Holly Cooper, Marc Brysbaert, Kathleen Rastle
pmc-12685991.description: A large portion of words in a language are formed by combining smaller meaningful units called morphemes (e.g., teach + -er → teacher). Understanding a language’s morphology is vital for skilled reading as it allows readers to interpret both familiar and unfamiliar words (e.g., tweeter).

pmc-13350115.title: Cross-Sector Policies for Achieving Equitable Obesity Prevention and Food Security: A Review of Real-World Actions
pmc-13350115.creator: Christina Zorbas, Sally Schultz, Shu Wen Ng, Erica Reeve, Ayuba Issaka, Chioma Anidi, Kathryn Backholer
pmc-13350115.description: Purpose of ReviewThis narrative review examines how government sectors beyond health contribute to the dual goals of equitable obesity prevention and food security through structural, cross‑sector policies. It aimed to synthesise real‑world evidence on the design, implementation and diet‑related impacts of policies across social, education, economic, trade and agricultural, and legal domains.

uslaw-usc-t11-s302.title: 11 U.S.C. § 302 — Joint cases
uslaw-usc-t11-s302.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t11-s302.description: United States Code, Title 11 (Bankruptcy); Chapter 3 (Case Administration); Subchapter I (Commencement Of A Case). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) A joint case under a chapter of this title is commenced by the filing with the bankruptcy court of a single petition under such chapter by an individual that may be a debtor under such chapter and such individual’s spouse.
